title: Interface Specification: the DMA enable and SPI-transmit-in-progress interface

standards_mappings.rationale: Backs SWE.2 with a real interface specification: providing and consuming module, the real C signature transcribed from the header at 308028fb, per-parameter direction, unit, meaning and valid range with the mechanism that enforces it, a return contract whose values are the enumerators the source defines, validity signalling read off the real error paths, timing where the source imposes one, concurrency, and a required not_specified_by_source list. Three elements, two of which record a declared-but-unimplemented interface, which is the finding rather than a gap in the record. The status stays partially_mapped: the whole family remains a reconstruction of an existing implementation rather than the product of an architectural design activity, and Component Design remains absent.

providing_module.name: DMA driver
providing_module.role: Configures and enables the DMA control packets used by the SPI, I2C and UART paths, and is the module a transmit-in-progress flag is expected to live in. Its public header is small: one initialiser and the two transmit-status accessors.

consuming_modules.name: SPI, I2C and UART drivers, and the AFE drivers
consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: The SPI boundary specified in FB2-SW-IFS-000008 depends on the DMA being initialised; the SPI boundary is anchored at src/app/driver/spi/spi.h L178-L186 and src/app/driver/spi/spi.c L513-L526. The AFE drivers call the transmit-status symbols that are actually defined, at src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6806/ltc_6806.c L650 and L723.

elements.consuming_module: Start-up, before the bus drivers use DMA

values.(no return value): The function returns nothing; it builds the DMA control packets and enables the DMA streams.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: A void initialiser for a resource that every serial bus later depends on gives no signal if it was never called or if a stream failed to enable.
return_contract.evidence: src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L74 declares void; src/app/driver/dma/dma.c L93 is the definition, building control packets for SPI at L95, SPI receive at L114 and I2C1 at L134 and ending at src/app/driver/dma/dma.c L170.

validity_signalling.mechanism: No return value. Nothing reports whether the streams were enabled.
validity_signalling.evidence: src/app/driver/dma/dma.c L93-L170 contains no return and no error result; the function signature is void.

timing.evidence: Called once at start-up, not periodically.

concurrency.evidence: A start-up initialiser writing module-static control packets; not re-entrant and unguarded.

error_paths.condition: a DMA stream fails to enable
error_paths.observed_behaviour: Not detected. The function is void and reports nothing.

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state which streams it enables, in what order relative to the bus drivers, or how a caller learns that DMA is available.
The header does not say that calling it more than once is unsafe, although it rebuilds the control packets unconditionally.

elements.providing_module: Declared in the DMA driver header; no implementation exists at this commit
elements.consuming_module: No caller at this commit calls this symbol

return_contract.default_on_no_information: The header documents the two values at src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L77-L79, but the function has no body anywhere in the source tree at 308028fb, so the interface promises a capability that is not implemented.
return_contract.evidence: The declaration is at src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L80 and the doc comment at L77-L79. A search of the whole tree at 308028fb finds DMA_IsTransmitOngoing only at that declaration; there is no definition.

validity_signalling.mechanism: The declared return value is a boolean, but there is no implementation, so the validity question is not reached: the symbol cannot be called.
validity_signalling.evidence: No definition exists at 308028fb; the only occurrence of the symbol in the tree is the declaration at src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L80.

concurrency.evidence: Nothing can be said about the calling context of a function that has no body; the header gives no context either.

error_paths.observed_behaviour: A link error, because no definition exists at 308028fb.
error_paths.evidence: The declaration at src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L80 is the only occurrence in the tree.

not_specified_by_source: The declaration has no implementation at 308028fb, so the interface as declared is not satisfiable; any caller would fail to link.

The symbols the AFE drivers actually use for this purpose are AFE_IsTransmitOngoing and AFE_SetTransmitOngoing, declared at src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.h L88 and L95 and defined at src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c L77 and L82. The header name and the implemented name do not correspond.
The interface does not say whether the flag is per-channel, per-bus or global, which is the first thing a caller would need to know.

elements.providing_module: Declared in the DMA driver header; no implementation exists at this commit
elements.consuming_module: No caller at this commit calls this symbol

values.(no return value): The function returns nothing; the header describes it as setting the SPI transmit status.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: Like its counterpart, the declared interface has no body at 308028fb.
return_contract.evidence: The declaration is at src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L85 and the doc comment at L82-L84. No definition exists in the tree at 308028fb.

validity_signalling.mechanism: None: the symbol cannot be called because it has no definition.
validity_signalling.evidence: The only occurrence of DMA_SetTransmitOngoing in the tree at 308028fb is the declaration at src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L85.

concurrency.evidence: No body and no context is stated in the header.

error_paths.observed_behaviour: A link error, because no definition exists at 308028fb.
error_paths.evidence: src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L85 is the only occurrence in the tree.

not_specified_by_source: The declaration has no implementation at 308028fb.

The implemented counterpart is AFE_SetTransmitOngoing at src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c L82, which takes an LTC_STATE_s pointer, so the header's zero-argument signature and the real function's signature do not match.
The interface does not state who clears the flag it sets.

interface_level_gaps.gap: Two functions declared in the public DMA header, DMA_IsTransmitOngoing and DMA_SetTransmitOngoing, have no definition anywhere in the source tree at 308028fb.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: The declared interface is not satisfiable. Any consumer that trusted the header and called either symbol would fail to link. The functionality exists, but under different names in a different module: AFE_IsTransmitOngoing and AFE_SetTransmitOngoing, which take an LTC_STATE_s pointer rather than none.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: A whole-tree search at 308028fb finds DMA_IsTransmitOngoing only at the declaration src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L80 and DMA_SetTransmitOngoing only at src/app/driver/dma/dma.h L85; the implemented symbols are at src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c L77 and L82.

interface_level_gaps.gap: The transmit-in-progress flag is scoped to the AFE module state rather than to the DMA, so the boundary that owns the DMA does not own the flag its header advertises.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: A caller of the DMA interface cannot reason about transmit-in-progress at all, because the flag lives in an AFE structure and the DMA header's version does not exist.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: The real flag is the transmit_ongoing field of LTC_STATE_s, read at src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c L79 and set at L84.

revision_history.description: Three elements over the DMA boundary, read from dma.h and dma.c at 308028fb. This record also carries the most concrete defect the extension found: two functions declared in dma.h, DMA_IsTransmitOngoing and DMA_SetTransmitOngoing, have no definition anywhere in the source tree at this commit, while the symbols the AFE drivers actually call are AFE_IsTransmitOngoing and AFE_SetTransmitOngoing in the AFE tree. The record states that rather than papering over it.
